title: Melania Trump's Amazon documentary deal
summary: The money is documented. Amazon paid about $40M for the 'Melania' rights (reported by Puck and the WSJ, not officially confirmed) plus about $35M in marketing, and the film grossed $16.6M. Trump's 2025 OGE report lists $10.71M of net proceeds from the film as spouse income, that is, Melania Trump's. Amazon and Bezos do have large business before the government: the FTC case and $2.5B settlement, AWS federal deals, Blue Origin launch awards, the Amazon Leo FCC waiver, and the tariff spat. The rival-bid figures (Disney about $14M, Paramount about $4M) rest on one anonymously sourced WSJ report, and the bribery or pay-to-play theory remains an unproven allegation by Democratic lawmakers, denied by Amazon, Bezos and Melania's office.

sub_claims.statement: Amazon paid about $40M to license the Melania documentary.
sub_claims.finding: Puck first reported it in Jan 2025 and the WSJ and others followed; Amazon confirmed the licensing deal (theatrical, Prime Video and a follow-up docuseries) but not the price. Amazon MGM reportedly spent about $35M more on marketing (about $75M total). The film opened Jan 30, 2026, took about $7M on opening weekend and about $16.6M globally, and has streamed on Prime since Mar 9, 2026. A two-part follow-up series is due Nov 20, 2026.

sub_claims.statement: Amazon's bid was far above rival bids.
sub_claims.finding: The WSJ reported Disney at about $14M and Paramount at about $4M, with Netflix and Apple not bidding, putting Amazon at nearly three times the next bid. Warren and Johnson cite a $26M gap over Disney. Puck and the Daily Beast said the losing bids were not public. Amazon called the process 'thorough and competitive' but did not disclose the rival bids. No primary confirmation was found.

sub_claims.statement: Melania netted about $10.7M+ from the film in 2025.
sub_claims.finding: Trump's 2025 OGE 278e (released 2026-06-30) lists the film fee in Part 5, 'Spouse's Employment Assets & Income', under MKT World LLC: 'License agreement with Designers Manager - Film "Melania"', net proceeds $10,710,000. It is therefore the First Lady's income reported on her husband's form, as Newsweek and Notus describe it; Variety and TheWrap's headlines call it Trump's. The same section lists $6,011,259 of net proceeds from NFTs and other collectibles and $521,161 from the Skyhorse memoir, $17,242,420 in all. The WSJ had reported her share at more than 70% of $40M (about $28M); the gap is unexplained and may be timing.

sub_claims.statement: Amazon and Bezos had major business before the administration (antitrust, cloud, Blue Origin/Kuiper, tariffs).
sub_claims.finding: FTC: the monopolization trial is set for 2027-03-29 (on 2026-10-09 the judge refused a further delay), and Amazon settled the Prime case on 2025-09-25 for $2.5B. AWS: the GSA OneGov deal (Aug 2025) and a $50B government AI infrastructure pledge (Nov 2025). Blue Origin: 7 NSSL missions worth about $2.3B (Apr 2025). Amazon Leo (formerly Kuiper): an FCC deadline waiver (Jun 2026). Tariffs: on 2025-04-29 the White House called a reported tariff-cost display 'hostile and political'; Trump said Bezos 'solved the problem very quickly'.

sub_claims.statement: The deal's timing lines up with government decisions favorable to Amazon.
sub_claims.finding: The chronology is real. Bezos dined with Trump at Mar-a-Lago in mid-Dec 2024, Amazon pledged $1M to the inauguration fund, and the deal was reported Jan 5-7, 2025, before the inauguration. Later actions (the FTC settlement, AWS and GSA deals, the NSSL award, the FCC waiver) followed. No document ties any decision to the film, the NSSL award was a multi-vendor competition, and the FTC antitrust case is still going to trial.

sub_claims.statement: Bezos/Amazon made an inauguration donation and Bezos changed the Washington Post's opinion section.
sub_claims.finding: Amazon gave $1M to the inauguration plus in-kind Prime streaming. On 2025-02-26 Bezos said Post opinion pages would defend 'personal liberties and free markets'; editor David Shipley left, and Ruth Marcus resigned in Mar 2025 after a critical column was killed. Linking these to the film is interpretation.

sub_claims.statement: The deal was a bribe or pay-to-play arrangement.
sub_claims.finding: Warren, Johnson, Lujan, Jayapal and Goldman wrote to Andy Jassy on 2026-03-15/16 citing possible bribery-law exposure. Amazon's VP Brian Huseman replied (reported as dated 2026-03-30) denying impropriety. On 2026-04-13 Warren called the deal 'bribery in plain sight'. No DOJ, IG or majority-led probe and no official finding was found.

corrections: The $10.71M appears on Donald Trump's 2025 OGE report, in Part 5 ('Spouse's Employment Assets & Income'), under Melania Trump's company MKT World LLC. It is her income, reported on his form; she files no separate report. Some headlines call it Trump's.
The rival bids (Disney about $14M, Paramount about $4M) come from one anonymously sourced WSJ report, never confirmed by Amazon.
Kuiper is now Amazon Leo; its 2026 FCC action was a deadline waiver, not a contract. Blue Origin's big federal award was the Apr 2025 NSSL launch contract (about $2.3B).
The WSJ reported Melania's share as more than 70% of $40M (about $28M), versus $10.71M disclosed for 2025. The two are not reconciled.

16 Nov 2026: Claimed: outlets are split on whether the $10.71M is Donald Trump's or Melania Trump's income. The record shows: the primary filing lists it in Part 5, spouse income, under MKT World LLC, so it is hers. Sub-claim 3 upgraded from mostly-accurate to confirmed.
denials_and_context: Amazon (VP Public Policy Brian Huseman): the bidding was 'thorough and competitive'; the choice rested on 'the access, the story, and its cultural and historical relevance'; nothing improper.
Jeff Bezos (CNBC, 2026-05-20): he had 'nothing to do with' the deal, the curry-favor claim is 'a falsehood that will not die', and the film was a 'very wise business decision'.
Marc Beckman (Melania's adviser): the film is 'not political at all'; Melania pitched it herself after the 2024 election.
Against the bribery theory: the FTC still got a record $2.5B Prime settlement and is taking the antitrust case to a 2027 trial; the NSSL awards went to three vendors.
Toward it: the film lost money theatrically (break-even about $40-45M domestic vs $16.6M global), yet Amazon ordered a follow-up series. Amazon is also a White House ballroom donor (see C33).
The official Warren and Hank Johnson pages and PDFs could not be read directly; their content is taken from outlets quoting them.

changes: No changes. The-Numbers gives a $16.56M worldwide gross, and Warren's own release and Amazon's response letter confirm the March and April 2026 exchange and the $26M gap over Disney. Bezos's 2026-05-20 CNBC Squawk Box defense ('a very wise business decision', 'nothing to do with it') is already in the file. The $10.71M OGE line was not re-verified independently.

16 Nov 2026: re-verified the $10.71M against the filing itself. It is in Part 5 (spouse income), MKT World LLC, net proceeds $10,710,000, next to $6,011,259 (NFTs) and $521,161 (memoir). Replaced the 'outlets split' caveat with the primary-document reading and upgraded sub-claim 3 to confirmed.
